sections.overview: The Least Tern is a small coastal tern that breeds in North America and parts of northern South America.
sections.identification: Adults are pale grey above and white below, with a black cap, yellow bill and dark bill tip in breeding plumage.
sections.habitat: It nests on open sand or gravel along beaches, estuaries and rivers, often where vegetation is sparse.
sections.diet: It catches small fish by hovering briefly and plunging into shallow water.
sections.behavior: Adults often defend the nesting area with repeated alarm calls and dives at intruders.
sections.reproduction: It lays its eggs in a shallow scrape on bare ground, with little or no nest material.
sections.ecology: Its nesting sites can be vulnerable to high tides; a Baja California study tested raising the nesting surface to reduce inundation.
sections.conservation: Conservation status varies by region and subspecies; a Mexican study describes local special protection and management of nesting habitat.
